title: Play, Go, Do: Sports
summary: Learn how to use play, go, and do with different sports. You will practice making correct sentences about hobbies.

sections.p: We use the verb play for team sports and games with a ball. These sports usually have a winner, a ball, and a team. For example, you play football with friends on the weekend. You also play tennis, basketball, and computer games.

ex.mean: I take part in a football game every Saturday.

sections.p: We use the verb go for activities that end in -ing. These are usually sports you do outside or move around a lot in, and you often do them alone or in a small group. For example, you go swimming, go running, and go cycling.

ex.en: She likes to go swimming in summer.
ex.mean: She enjoys swimming when the weather is warm.
I want us to run together today.

sections.p: We use the verb do for individual exercises and martial arts. These are fitness activities or sports that do not use a ball and usually do not end in -ing. For example, you do yoga, do karate, and do gymnastics to stay strong and healthy.

ex.mean: I practice yoga daily to feel relaxed.

ex.en: He does judo at the school club.
ex.mean: He practices judo with his school.

words.mean: used for fitness and martial arts
team sport with a round ball
sport with a hoop and ball

tip: Remember: ball sports = play, -ing words = go, and gym/martial arts = do. Say the rules out loud three times!

quiz.en: I want to ___ basketball with my friends.
My brother likes to ___ swimming every weekend.
She wants to ___ karate after school.
